# DatePicker

<!-- Generated by `pnpm readme:build`. Edit only inside the hand-written block. -->

forms · tier 3 · beta · runs in the browser.

<!-- hand-written -->

## When to use

For one day, picked from a month: a check-in, a due date, a birthday a few years back. It is one
element: a button that shows the day, and a calendar that opens under it. No date library: the
grid is ours and every word and digit comes from `Intl`.

```tsx
import { DatePicker } from 'topclassui'
```

```tsx
<label htmlFor="check-in">Check-in</label>
<DatePicker id="check-in" name="checkIn" defaultValue="2026-10-02" minDate="2026-09-25" maxDate="2027-03-31" />
```

**In a Field** the control object spreads onto it as it is:

```tsx
<Field name="checkIn" label="Check-in" hint="Rooms are ready from 15:00">
  {(control) => <DatePicker {...control} defaultValue="2026-10-02" />}
</Field>
```

**A name is required.** `id` for a `<label htmlFor>`, or `aria-label`, or `aria-labelledby`; the
type refuses a DatePicker with none. The label names the button and the day is its description,
read after it. While the calendar is open Base UI hides the rest of the page from readers, the
label too; the focus is in the calendar then, named by its month, and the label is back on close.

**The value is an ISO date**, `YYYY-MM-DD`, a string: `value`, `defaultValue` (a string or `null`)
and `onValueChange(value)`. A string that is not a real day (`2026-02-30`) counts as `null`.
Nothing chosen shows `placeholder`, or `datePicker.placeholder` from the provider's labels.

**The form.** With a `name`, a hidden input sends `name=2026-10-02`, and `name=` with nothing
chosen. Before the page hydrates it sends the default. A form reset, a reset button or a React 19
form action that settles brings back the `defaultValue` of the latest render. After a choice the
input fires an `input` event, so a FieldLive and your own listeners hear it. **`required`** with
nothing chosen blocks a submit; the button is described as required, since a button cannot carry
`aria-required`. Before the page hydrates the browser then puts the focus on the hidden input, a
box of 1 px; after it, on the button.

**`minDate` and `maxDate`** are ISO dates, `0001-01-01` and `9999-12-31` by default and at most.
A date that is not real takes the bound, and `maxDate` below `minDate` is raised to it. A day
outside is dimmed and cannot be chosen; the month buttons stop at them. A `value` outside the
range is kept, shown and sent as given; the calendar opens on it, and the first key brings the
active day into the range.

**The week** starts on `firstDayOfWeek`, 1 (Monday) to 7 (Sunday), rounded and clamped; left out,
on the locale's first day, read in the browser (Sunday in `en`, Monday in `en-GB`, Saturday in
`ar`), and Monday where the browser has none.

**The keyboard** (the Authoring Practices date picker dialog). The calendar opens with the focus
on the chosen day, else on today. The arrows move a day and a week; in Arabic ArrowLeft is the
next day. Home and End go to the first and the last day of the row, within the month. PageUp and
PageDown move a month, with Shift a year, keeping the day inside the month (31 March back is
28 February). Enter or Space chooses and closes; Escape closes with no change; the focus returns
to the button. Tab goes round previous, next, close and the grid.

**Today** is the browser's own calendar day, read when the calendar opens; it is underlined and
heavier. The chosen day is filled and heavier. Under forced colours the chosen day takes the
`Highlight` pair and today keeps its underline.

**Words and digits** come from the nearest `TopClassProvider`: the month and the day names from
`Intl` in its `locale`, the digits in its numbering system (`ar` with Latin digits by default,
Arabic-Indic with `numberingSystem="arab"`). The grid is always Gregorian.

**The calendar loads on the first open**: the popup and its grid are a chunk of their own, and on
that first open the popup appears once the chunk has arrived, whole. Its keys, the date math and
the formatters load with the button.

**The width** belongs to a box around the button, as on Select: an Input's width at the same
`size`, less in a narrower parent; `fullWidth` fills the parent.

**The popup** is 280 px, never wider than the screen, and scrolls itself on a short one.
`placement` takes the twelve shared values, `bottom-start` by default, 6 px off the button and 8 px
inside the screen. Escape closes the calendar first, then a Dialog around it. It takes its
direction and language from the provider, also in an island.

**On a phone** a day is 44 px tall and about 31 px wide at 320 px: the seven columns of a 280 px
popup cannot reach 44 px each.

**On the element.** `className`, `style`, `ref`, `aria-describedby`, `aria-invalid` and the rest go
to the button. `invalid` sets `aria-invalid`: the line turns red and thickens. `disabled` is the real
attribute, on the button and the input, so the form sends nothing. `open`, `defaultOpen` and
`onOpenChange` are Base UI's, on the root.

### What Base UI gives

| Base UI | Here |
|---|---|
| `Popover.Root`, `Trigger`, `Portal`, `Positioner`, `Popup`, `Title`, `Close` | one `DatePicker` |
| `open`, `defaultOpen`, `onOpenChange` | passed through; Escape is guarded per root |
| `modal` | always `'trap-focus'`, with the `Close` part that makes the trap work |
| `side`, `align`, `sideOffset`, `collisionPadding` | `placement` and the shared offsets |
| `container` on the Portal | passed through |
| the trigger's `render`, `nativeButton`, `handle`, `payload`, `openOnHover`, `delay`, `closeDelay` | not props |

### Not built

Hijri and every other calendar, a range (DateRangePicker), week numbers, a clear or a today
button, a text input to type a date, a time, `isDateDisabled`, a month or year menu, two months
side by side, `readOnly`, `keepMounted`, a Drawer on a phone (AdaptiveDatePicker), a `locale`
prop (the provider's), the drawn open look of the button, a skeleton (use `InputSkeleton`).

## Import

```tsx
import { DatePicker } from 'topclassui'
```

## Props

Required: `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby` or `id`. Every other prop below is optional.

| Prop | Required | Type | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `aria-label` | **yes**, or `aria-labelledby` or `id` | `string` | - | The name read out when no visible label names the control. |
| `aria-labelledby` | **yes**, or `aria-label` or `id` | `string` | - | The id of the visible text that names the control. |
| `id` | **yes**, or `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby` | `string` | - | The id a `<label htmlFor>` points at. |
| `className` | no | `string` | - | On the trigger, merged last, so a consumer class wins a conflict with its own. |
| `container` | no | `Base.Portal.Props['container']` | - | Where the calendar mounts; `<body>` by default. |
| `defaultValue` | no | `string \| null` | - | The day of the first render, and the one a form reset brings back. |
| `firstDayOfWeek` | no | `number`, min 1, max 7 | - | DatePicker: the first column, 1 (Monday) to 7 (Sunday), rounded and clamped; left out, the locale's. |
| `form` | no | `string` | - | The id of a form elsewhere on the page that the form input belongs to. |
| `fullWidth` | no | `boolean` | `false` | DatePicker: the box fills the width of its parent instead of taking the width of an Input. |
| `invalid` | no | `boolean` | `false` | DatePicker: marks the date as wrong: sets aria-invalid on the trigger, whose line turns to danger and thickens. |
| `maxDate` | no | `string` | `"9999-12-31"` | DatePicker: the last day that can be chosen, clamped like minDate and raised to it when below. |
| `minDate` | no | `string` | `"0001-01-01"` | DatePicker: the first day that can be chosen, an ISO date clamped to 0001-01-01 to 9999-12-31. |
| `name` | no | `string` | - | The form input's name: the form sends `name=YYYY-MM-DD`, and `name=` when empty. |
| `onValueChange` | no | `((value: string) => void)` | - | Called with the ISO date of the day chosen. |
| `placeholder` | no | `string` | - | The text of an empty trigger. Left out, the provider's `datePicker.placeholder`. |
| `placement` | no | `top` \| `top-start` \| `top-end` \| `bottom` \| `bottom-start` \| `bottom-end` \| `start` \| `start-top` \| `start-bottom` \| `end` \| `end-top` \| `end-bottom` | `"bottom-start"` | DatePicker: the side and alignment the calendar opens at; start and end mirror in Arabic. |
| `ref` | no | `Ref<HTMLButtonElement>` | - | The trigger, a `<button aria-haspopup="dialog">`. |
| `required` | no | `boolean` | - | Blocks an empty submit, with or without script; the trigger is described as required. |
| `size` | no | `xs` \| `sm` \| `md` \| `lg` \| `xl` \| `custom` | `"md"` | DatePicker: the height, the inline padding and the type step of the trigger, and its width with them; custom emits no size classes. |
| `value` | no | `string \| null` | - | The chosen day as an ISO date, `YYYY-MM-DD`, or null. A string that is not a real day counts as null. |

Anything else is passed to the root element, so standard attributes (`onClick`, `aria-*`, `data-*`, `id`) work. `className` is merged last, so yours wins a conflict, and `ref` is a normal prop.
